scope.supportedBoundary: Offline, read-only, single-repository architecture queries with explicit selectors, bounded traversal, evidence-linked paths, impact explanations, metadata projections, and declared resource limits.
scope.unsupportedBoundary: Multi-repository composition, production reviewer behavior, universal precision claims, unbounded traversal, source execution, network retrieval, and absolute-path or source-body reporting remain outside this gate.

thresholds.rationale: Every declared query-contract case must remain correct and repeatable.
Affected-set overreach must stay below the declared single-repository review floor.
Supported impact paths must recover the declared affected records.
Every explanation case must expose inspectable paths, evidence, uncertainty, limits, and tool metadata.
Declared node, edge, depth, report, memory, and wall-clock limits must produce typed bounded outcomes.
Invalid requests must fail closed without executing or mutating a graph.

thresholds.unit: path and source disclosure checks passed
thresholds.rationale: Reports must not expose absolute paths, source bodies, secrets, remote fetches, or executable resources.
At least four representative reviewer tasks are required before team-scale composition.
The same canonical inputs must serialize identically across repeated local runs.
Team-scale composition requires evidence beyond the bounded single-repository corpus.

measurements.notes: All 14 query-contract cases passed, including positive, unsupported, resource-limit, malformed, path, cycle, and metadata outcomes.
The six-case Q-004 corpus reports 16 true positives and two declared overreach records, for precision 0.8888888888888888.
The Q-004 corpus recovered all 16 expected affected records with no false negatives.
All five Q-005 cases produced complete JSON, Markdown, and HTML explanations with expected uncertainty, limits, evidence, and metadata.
Over-limit query cases return the declared resource-limit state; the local contract enforces bounded depth, nodes, edges, output, memory, and wall-clock resources.
Malformed requests are rejected with a typed validation error, and the validator proves the graph remains unchanged.

measurements.unit: path and source disclosure checks passed
measurements.notes: The report and explanation evaluators reject absolute paths, source-body fields, remote references, executable resources, and secret markers.
Three of four bounded reviewer tasks completed; the impact-overreach task remains partial because the precision floor is missed.
Impact and explanation evaluators compare repeated serialized output and fail on any digest or ordering drift.
The checked-in corpus is single-repository and synthetic; no workspace composition or external reviewer replication evidence is present.

reviewerTasks.expected: Identify the selected path, cycle, boundary, evidence, and uncertainty without reading source bodies.
reviewerTasks.notes: The explanation includes the normalized plan, path, cycle, evidence, and truncation details.

reviewerTasks.expected: Distinguish expected affected records from boundary-stop and unresolved-edge overreach.
reviewerTasks.notes: The reasons are visible, but the measured precision is below the declared quality floor.

reviewerTasks.expected: Locate policy, ADR, ownership, empty-result, and missing-evidence context in a self-contained report.
reviewerTasks.notes: JSON, Markdown, and HTML projections expose the expected context and accessibility landmarks.

reviewerTasks.expected: Recognize malformed and over-limit outcomes as safe fail-closed states rather than empty success.
reviewerTasks.notes: The corpus distinguishes invalid, resource-limit, unsupported, and successful outcomes.

limitations.description: The Q-004 synthetic impact corpus has two declared overreach records and precision below the 0.90 gate floor, so broad impact claims would be misleading.
Whole-repository adapter and language-equivalence runs can hit the configured 536870912-byte RSS ceiling; this gate does not convert a bounded-resource outcome into a scale guarantee.
Reviewer tasks are repository-authored synthetic scenarios rather than independent external user studies.
No workspace manifest, cross-repository identity, trust, or missing-repository composition evidence is included, so team-scale composition remains deferred.

decision.rationale: Continue the bounded, offline, single-repository query and explanation slice, but narrow impact claims because precision is 0.8888888888888888 against a 0.90 floor and one reviewer task remains partial. Defer multi-repository composition because the current evidence has no workspace trust, identity, omission, or independent reviewer replication coverage.
decision.continueScope: Keep deterministic, read-only, source-free query selection and inspectable explanations available for one bounded repository with explicit limits and visible uncertainty.
decision.narrowScope: Treat impact output as review assistance, surface boundary-stop and unresolved-edge overreach, and require human confirmation whenever the precision floor or reviewer task floor is missed.
decision.deferScope: Do not claim team-scale or multi-repository composition until workspace identity, trust, missing-input, resource, and independent reviewer-utility evidence are measured in a follow-up gate.

provenance.source: CARTOGRAPH repository-authored measurements from Q-003, Q-004, and Q-005 local validators
